Subsequent slices drain via\\n        // `take_pending_structural_section(prefix)`.\\n        for (k, v) in outcome.structural {\\n            self.pending_config_structural_sections.insert(k, v);\\n        }\\n        // Surface a single echo summarising loader diagnostics.\\n        // The renderer's modeline only shows the latest echo,\\n        // so multi-warn configs collapse into \\\"<count> issues\\n        // (first: <body>)\\\". Severity is the max across the run.\\n        if outcome.messages.is_empty() {\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        let max_level = outcome\\n            .messages\\n            .iter()\\n            .map(|m| m.level)\\n            .max_by_key(|l| match l {\\n                lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Error => 1,\\n                lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Warning => 0,\\n            })\\n            .unwrap_or(lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Warning);\\n        let echo_level = match max_level {\\n            lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Error => EchoLevel::Error,\\n            lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Warning => EchoLevel::Warn,\\n        };\\n        let count = outcome.messages.len();\\n        let first = &outcome.messages[0];\\n        let body = if count == 1 {\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"config: {}: {}\\\",\\n                first.source.display(),\\n                first.body,\\n            )\\n        } else {\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"config: {count} issues (first: {}: {})\\\",\\n                first.source.display(),\\n                first.body,\\n            )\\n        };\\n        self.set_message(echo_level, body);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Drain every `completion.per-language.<lang>` structural\\n    /// section the loader bucketed and merge each into\\n    /// `self.per_language_completion`. Per-key TOML wins over\\n    /// the spec defaults seeded at `App::new`; unset keys leave\\n    /// the default in place.\\n    ///\\n    /// Called by the runtime startup right after\\n    /// `load_persistent_config` finishes. Idempotent (the bucket\\n    /// empties as we drain). Per-key parse warnings collapse\\n    /// into a single echo at `Warn` level the same way the\\n    /// loader's other diagnostics do.\\n    pub fn apply_per_language_toml_overrides(&mut self) {\\n        let paths = self.pending_structural_section_paths(\\\"completion.per-language\\\");\\n        let mut warnings: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\\n        for path in paths {\\n            let lang = match path.strip_prefix(\\\"completion.per-language.\\\") {\\n                Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => s.to_string(),\\n                _ => continue,\\n            };\\n            let Some(table) = self.take_pending_structural_section(&path) else {\\n                continue;\\n            };\\n            let parsed = parse_per_language_overrides_table(&path, &table, &mut warnings);\\n            self.per_language_completion\\n                .entry(lang)\\n                .or_default()\\n                .merge(parsed);\\n        }\\n        if !warnings.is_empty() {\\n            let count = warnings.len();\\n            let body = if count == 1 {\\n                format!(\\\"config: {}\\\", warnings[0])\\n            } else {\\n                format!(\\\"config: {count} per-language warnings (first: {})\\\", warnings[0])\\n            };\\n            self.set_message(EchoLevel::Warn, body);\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Effective completion config for `language` -- per-language\\n    /// override lays over the global typed option which lays\\n    /// over the spec fallback. Used by the per-language /\\n    /// plugin-host layers to consume their TOML config without\\n    /// leaving stale entries behind.\\n    pub fn take_pending_structural_section(\\n        &mut self,\\n        full_path: &str,\\n    ) -> Option<toml::Table> {\\n        self.pending_config_structural_sections.remove(full_path)\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Iterate the dotted paths of every pending structural\\n    /// section whose path starts with `namespace.` (e.g.\\n    /// `\\\"completion.per-language\\\"` returns the language ids).\\n    /// Returned as owned `String`s to keep the borrow short --\\n    /// callers typically follow up with\\n    /// `take_pending_structural_section(full)` mutating the map.\\n    pub fn pending_structural_section_paths(\\n        &self,\\n        namespace: &str,\\n    ) -> Vec<String> {\\n        let prefix = format!(\\\"{namespace}.\\\");\\n        self.pending_config_structural_sections\\n            .keys()\\n            .filter(|k| k.starts_with(&prefix))\\n            .cloned()\\n            .collect()\\n    }\\n\\n    fn do_set(&mut self, option: &str) {\\n        let echo = match self.config.parse_and_set_command(option) {\\n            Ok(echo) => echo,\\n            Err(err) => {\\n                self.set_message(EchoLevel::Error, err.to_string());\\n                return;\\n            }\\n        };\\n        // Drain any cascade events the set just enqueued so the\\n        // user sees the side effects (recompute folds, theme\\n        // refresh, ...) before the next frame draws. The runtime's\\n        // main_loop also drains once per iteration as a backstop\\n        // for writes that originate outside the keystroke path\\n        // (plugin tasks, future LSP-driven config writes).\\n        self.drain_option_changes();\\n        self.set_message(EchoLevel::Info, echo);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Drain queued [`Event::OptionChanged`] events from the App's\\n    /// own bus subscription and apply per-option cascades on the\\n    /// App's main thread.\\n    ///\\n    /// Why a channel and not a callback: typed-option writes can\\n    /// originate from anywhere -- the cmdline, plugin tasks\\n    /// (Phase 7), the customize buffer view (post-1.0), or future\\n    /// LSP-driven config writes. Pre-bus the cascade lived\\n    ///   on the cmdline path only and direct `config.set` calls\\n    ///   silently skipped it.\\n    ///\\n    /// `Manual` foldmethod, no-op cascades, and unmatched options\\n    /// all return early so the drain is cheap when nothing\\n    /// substantive needs to happen.\\n    pub fn drain_option_changes(&mut self) {\\n        // Take the receiver to dodge the borrow checker (we want\\n        // to mutate `self` for cascades while reading from the rx).\\n        // Always restored after the loop; the `Option` is purely a\\n        // borrow gymnastic, never observed in any other state.\\n        let mut rx = match self.option_change_rx.take() {\\n            Some(rx) => rx,\\n            None => return,\\n        };\\n        while let Ok(event) = rx.try_recv() {\\n            if let Event::OptionChanged { name, .. } = event {\\n                self.apply_option_cascade(&name);\\n            }\\n        }\\n        self.option_change_rx = Some(rx);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Run the per-option cascade for `canonical_name` (already\\n    /// resolved by `Event::OptionChanged.name`, which is always\\n    /// the canonical name regardless of which alias the user\\n    /// typed).\\n    fn apply_option_cascade(&mut self, canonical_name: &str) {\\n        // Refresh the hot-path cache so subsequent reads from\\n        // `app.show_line_numbers()` etc. see the new value.\\n        // Cheap (~300ns total for all 9 options); only runs when\\n        // an option actually changed, never on every frame.\\n        self.rebuild_option_cache();\\n        match canonical_name {\\n            \\\"relativenumber\\\" => {\\n                // Vim cascade: `:set rnu` implies `:set nu` so the\\n                // gutter renders at all. Idempotent\\n                // and cheap when method is `Manual` (the recompute\\n                // returns immediately).\\n                self.recompute_folds();\\n            }\\n            n if n.starts_with(\\\"ui.\\\") => {\\n                self.sync_theme_from_config();\\n            }\\n            _ => {}\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Re-derive `App.theme`'s renderer-specific [`Style`] values\\n    /// from the current `ui.*` option values in the config. Called\\n    /// at App-init time (after registration) and on every `:set\\n    /// ui.*` so the cached theme stays in lockstep with the\\n    /// canonical primitives in config.\\n    pub fn sync_theme_from_config(&mut self) {\\n        use ratatui::style::Style;\\n        // ui.dim_inactive -- bool flag projected directly.\\n        self.theme.dim_inactive_panes = *self.config.get(self.tui_options.dim_inactive);\\n        // ui.separator -- one-character glyph for the vertical\\n        // pane divider. Validated to len==1 at parse; fall back to\\n        // the default if a forged value sneaks through.\\n        let sep = self.config.get(self.tui_options.separator);\\n        self.theme.pane_separator_vertical = sep.chars().next().unwrap_or('│');\\n        // ui.separator_color -- color name; parse_color returned\\n        // Ok during validate so unwrap-via-fallback is safe.\\n        let sep_color = self.config.get(self.tui_options.separator_color);\\n        if let Ok(c) = crate::theme::parse_color(&sep_color) {\\n            self.theme.pane_separator = Style::default().fg(c);\\n        }\\n        // ui.statusline_active_fg -- foreground only; preserve any\\n        // existing modifiers / background by chaining `.fg(c)` on\\n        // the current style.\\n        let active_fg = self.config.get(self.tui_options.statusline_active_fg);\\n        if let Ok(c) = crate::theme::parse_color(&active_fg) {\\n            self.theme.pane_status_active = self.theme.pane_status_active.fg(c);\\n        }\\n        let inactive_fg = self.config.get(self.tui_options.statusline_inactive_fg);\\n        if let Ok(c) = crate::theme::parse_color(&inactive_fg) {\\n            self.theme.pane_status_inactive = self.theme.pane_status_inactive.fg(c);\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// `:describe-option <name>` (DESIGN.md §5.11). Renders the\\n    /// option's metadata + current value into a help buffer.\\n    fn do_describe_option(&mut self, name: &str) {\\n        let Some(spec) = self.config.lookup(name) else {\\n            self.set_message(EchoLevel::Error, format!(\\\"E518: Unknown option: {name}\\\"));\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\\n        lines.push(format!(\\\"# {}\\\", spec.name()));\\n        if !spec.aliases().is_empty() {\\n            lines.push(format!(\\\"aliases: {}\\\", spec.aliases().join(\\\", \\\")));\\n        }\\n        lines.push(format!(\\\"type:    {}\\\", spec.type_label()));\\n        lines.push(format!(\\\"default: {}\\\", spec.default_formatted()));\\n        lines.push(format!(\\\"current: {}\\\", spec.get_formatted()));\\n        if let Some(values) = spec.enumerate_values() {\\n            lines.push(format!(\\\"values:  {}\\\", values.join(\\\", \\\")));\\n        }\\n        lines.push(String::new());\\n        lines.push(spec.doc().to_string());\\n        self.open_help(\\n            HelpBuffer::from_lines(format!(\\\"describe-option {name}\\\"), lines)\\n                .with_markdown_syntax(self.lang_registry.clone()),\\n        );\\n    }\\n\\n    /// `K` (LSP hover) response handler / `:hover [markdown]`.\\n    /// Enters **State A**: popup overlay shown, focus stays on\\n    /// the main buffer. The active buffer is tagged `(current)` in the\\n/// marginalia and floated to the bottom so the picker's\\n/// initial-selected row lands on the alternate buffer (vim's\\n/// `:b<CR>` shortcut).\\npub(crate) fn raw_buffer_candidates(\\n    registry: &BufferRegistry,\\n    active: BufferId,\\n) -> Vec<(lattice_completion::RawCandidate, crate::picker::RoutingPayload)> {\\n    let mut ids = registry.sorted_ids();\\n    ids.sort_by_key(|id| (*id == active, *id));\\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(ids.len());\\n    for id in ids {\\n        let Some(entry) = registry.get(id) else {\\n            continue;\\n        };\\n        let active_marker = if id == active { \\\" (current)\\\" } else { \\\"\\\" };\\n        let (body, kind_label) = match &entry.data {\\n            BufferData::Document(d) => {\\n                let path = d\\n                    .handle\\n                    .path()\\n                    .map(|p| p.display().to_string())\\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \\\"[no name]\\\".to_string());\\n                let dirty = if d.handle.dirty() { \\\" [+]\\\" } else { \\\"\\\" };\\n                (\\n                    format!(\\\"#{:<3} {path}{dirty}\\\", id.0),\\n                    format!(\\\"doc{active_marker}\\\"),\\n                )\\n            }\\n            BufferData::FileTree(t) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, t.root.display()),\\n                format!(\\\"tree{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n            BufferData::Help(h) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, h.title),\\n                format!(\\\"help{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n            BufferData::Oil(o) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, o.dir.display()),\\n                format!(\\\"oil{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n        };\\n        // `text` is the user-facing buffer id; matcher matches\\n        // against `display`. For 4.2.b utf-16 is correct\\n/// for every server we care about today.\\n/// Render an LSP `SignatureHelp` response into a markdown body\\n/// the popup renderer can display. Picks the active signature\\n/// (server-supplied `active_signature` index, default 0) and\\n/// inlines the active parameter's documentation when present.\\n/// Returns the empty string when the response carries no\\n/// signatures.\\npub(crate) fn signature_help_to_markdown(sh: &lsp_types::SignatureHelp) -> String {\\n    if sh.signatures.is_empty() {\\n        return String::new();\\n    }\\n    let active_sig_idx = sh.active_signature.unwrap_or(0) as usize;\\n    let sig = sh\\n        .signatures\\n        .get(active_sig_idx)\\n        .or_else(|| sh.signatures.first())\\n        .expect(\\\"non-empty checked above\\\");\\n    let mut out = String::new();\\n    // Active signature's call form -- renders as a fenced code\\n    // block so the popup's markdown highlighter picks up\\n    // syntax highlighting (whatever language the server says\\n    // -- we don't know, so default to text).\\n    out.push_str(\\\"```text\\\\n\\\");\\n    out.push_str(&sig.label);\\n    out.push_str(\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\");\\n    // Parameter highlight: append a short note pointing at the\\n    // active parameter's name. The popup overlay doesn't yet\\n    // do per-character paragraph styling, so this is the\\n    // friendliest representation we have without bespoke\\n    // rendering.\\n    if let Some(active_param_idx) = sig.active_parameter.or(sh.active_parameter)\\n        && let Some(params) = sig.parameters.as_ref()\\n        && let Some(param) = params.get(active_param_idx as usize)\\n    {\\n        let label_str = match &param.label {\\n            lsp_types::ParameterLabel::Simple(s) => s.clone(),\\n            lsp_types::ParameterLabel::LabelOffsets(_) => String::new(),\\n        };\\n        if !label_str.is_empty() {\\n            out.push_str(&format!(\\\"\\\\n**param:** `{label_str}`\\\\n\\\"));\\n        }\\n        if let Some(doc) = param.documentation.as_ref() {\\n            let doc_str = match doc {\\n                lsp_types::Documentation::String(s) => s.clone(),\\n                lsp_types::Documentation::MarkupContent(mc) => mc.value.clone(),\\n            };\\n            if !doc_str.is_empty() {\\n                out.push('\\\\n');\\n                out.push_str(&doc_str);\\n                out.push('\\\\n');\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n    // Signature-level documentation when present.\\n    if let Some(doc) = sig.documentation.as_ref() {\\n        let doc_str = match doc {\\n            lsp_types::Documentation::String(s) => s.clone(),\\n            lsp_types::Documentation::MarkupContent(mc) => mc.value.clone(),\\n        };\\n        if !doc_str.is_empty() {\\n            out.push('\\\\n');\\n            out.push_str(&doc_str);\\n            out.push('\\\\n');\\n        }\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\n/// Inverse of `app_to_lsp_position` -- LSP utf-16 character\\n/// column → utf-8 byte column on the given line. Used by\\n/// `apply_lsp_text_edits` to convert TextEdit ranges back to\\n/// the App's `Position` shape.\\npub(crate) fn lsp_position_to_app_byte(buffer: &Buffer, line: u32, character: u32) -> u32 {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(line).unwrap_or_default();\\n    lattice_lsp::position::utf16_column_to_utf8_byte(&line_text, character)\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn app_to_lsp_position(buffer: &Buffer, p: Position) -> Option<lsp_types::Position> {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(p.line)?;\\n    let character = lattice_lsp::position::utf8_byte_to_utf16_column(&line_text, p.byte);\\n    Some(lsp_types::Position {\\n        line: p.line,\\n        character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `DocumentSymbolResponse` into our pre-rendered\\n/// `SymbolRow` shape. The legacy `Flat(Vec<SymbolInformation>)`\\n/// variant is one row per symbol with no nesting; the modern\\n/// `Nested(Vec<DocumentSymbol>)` variant carries\\n/// `children: Vec<DocumentSymbol>`, walked depth-first to\\n/// preserve outline ordering.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_document_symbol_response(\\n    resp: lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse,\\n    path: &std::path::Path,\\n    out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n) {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Flat(syms) => {\\n            for sym in syms {\\n                if let Some(row) = symbol_information_to_row(&sym) {\\n                    out.push(row);\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Nested(syms) => {\\n            fn walk(\\n                syms: Vec<lsp_types::DocumentSymbol>,\\n                path: &std::path::Path,\\n                depth: u32,\\n                out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n            ) {\\n                for sym in syms {\\n                    out.push(SymbolRow {\\n                        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n                        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n                        container: None,\\n                        depth,\\n                        path: path.to_path_buf(),\\n                        line: sym.selection_range.start.line,\\n                        col: sym.selection_range.start.character,\\n                    });\\n                    if let Some(children) = sym.children {\\n                        walk(children, path, depth + 1, out);\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            }\\n            walk(syms, path, 0, out);\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Map a flat `SymbolInformation` (legacy outline + workspace\\n/// symbol shape) into our row type. Returns `None` when the\\n/// location's URI doesn't resolve to a path.\\npub(crate) fn symbol_information_to_row(\\n    sym: &lsp_types::SymbolInformation,\\n) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&sym.location.uri)?;\\n    Some(SymbolRow {\\n        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n        container: sym.container_name.clone(),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: sym.location.range.start.line,\\n        col: sym.location.range.start.character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// Extract a placeholder string from a `PrepareRenameResponse`.\\n/// The spec gives three shapes: a Range (no placeholder, just\\n/// \\\"you can rename here\\\"), a Range+Placeholder (preferred), or\\n/// a DefaultBehavior signal (server defers to the editor's\\n/// word-under-cursor heuristic). We pull the placeholder when\\n/// present, else `None` so the App's caller can fall back to\\n/// the heuristic.\\npub(crate) fn prepare_rename_placeholder(\\n    resp: &lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse,\\n) -> Option<String> {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::RangeWithPlaceholder { placeholder, .. } => {\\n            Some(placeholder.clone())\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::Range(_) => None,\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::DefaultBehavior { .. } => None,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `WorkspaceEdit` into a per-file\\n/// `Vec<(Uri, Vec<TextEdit>)>`. On miss the echo\\n    /// lists running actor ids so the user sees what's available\\n    /// instead of a phantom-toggle that goes nowhere.\\n    pub fn do_toggle_lsp_trace(&mut self, name: &str) {\\n        let resolved = self.resolve_server_id(name);\\n        let Some(server_id) = resolved else {\\n            let running = self.running_server_ids();\\n            let listing = if running.is_empty() {\\n                \\\"no LSP servers running\\\".to_string()\\n            } else {\\n                format!(\\\"running: {}\\\", running.join(\\\", \\\"))\\n            };\\n            self.set_message(\\n                EchoLevel::Error,\\n                format!(\\\"lsp-trace: no server matches {name:?} ({listing})\\\"),\\n            );\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let id: std::sync::Arc<str> = std::sync::Arc::from(server_id.as_str());\\n        let now_on = self.lsp_logger.toggle_trace(id);\\n        let label = if now_on { \\\"on\\\" } else { \\\"off\\\" };\\n        let alias_note = if server_id != name {\\n            format!(\\\" (resolved {name:?} -> {server_id:?})\\\")\\n        } else {\\n            String::new()\\n        };\\n        self.set_message(\\n            EchoLevel::Info,\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"lsp-trace {server_id}: {label}{alias_note} (use :lsp-trace-log {server_id} to view)\\\"\\n            ),\\n        );\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Resolve a user-supplied server name to a canonical server\\n    /// id. self.publish_document_changed();\\n        }\\n        result\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn redo_blocking(&self) -> Result<Vec<AppliedEdit>, RuntimeError> {\\n        let result = When the\\n    /// server requested `includeText`, attach the post-save\\n    /// text from the rope.\\n    fn fire_did_save_notifications(&self) {\\n        let Some(uri) = self.buffer_uris.get(&self.document_buffer_id) else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let lsp = self.lsp.clone();\\n        let uri = uri.clone();\\n        let handles = match lsp.try_lock() {\\n            Ok(g) => g.servers_for(&uri),\\n            Err(_) => return,\\n        };\\n        let snap = self.document.snapshot();\\n        let full_text = snap.buffer.as_string();\\n        for h in handles {\\n            let caps = h.capabilities();\\n            if !caps.wants_did_save() {\\n                continue;\\n            }\\n            let text = if caps.did_save_include_text() {\\n                Some(full_text.clone())\\n            } else {\\n                None\\n            };\\n            let params = lsp_types::DidSaveTextDocumentParams {\\n                text_document: lsp_types::TextDocumentIdentifier {\\n                    uri: uri.clone(),\\n                },\\n                text,\\n            };\\n            let _ = h.did_save(params);\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn save_as_blocking(&self, path: std::path::PathBuf) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {\\n        let snap = self.document.snapshot();\\n        self.event_bus.publish(Event::BeforeSave {\\n            id: snap.id,\\n            path: path.clone(),\\n        });\\n        let result = block_on(self.document.save_as(path.clone()));\\n        if result.is_ok() {\\n            self.event_bus\\n                .publish(Event::DocumentSaved { id: snap.id, path });\\n        }\\n        result\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn set_selections_blocking(&self, selections: SelectionSet) {\\n        // SetSelections only fails on actor-gone; ignore the\\n        // Result (post-shutdown nothing meaningful to do).\\n        let _ = block_on(self.document.set_selections(selections));\\n        self.publish_selections_changed();\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Build + publish [`Event::DocumentChanged`] from the current\\n    /// snapshot. Innermost = max start_line, then min end_line on ties.\\n/// Used by `zc` (close innermost open) and `za`'s close branch.\\nfn innermost_fold_idx<F: Fn(&Fold) -> bool>(\\n    folds: &[Fold],\\n    line: u32,\\n    pred: F,\\n) -> Option<usize> {\\n    folds\\n        .iter()\\n        .enumerate()\\n        .filter(|(_, f)| pred(f) && line >= f.start_line && line <= f.end_line)\\n        .max_by_key(|(_, f)| (f.start_line, std::cmp::Reverse(f.end_line)))\\n        .map(|(i, _)| i)\\n}\\n\\n/// Pick the fold that `zc` (or `za`'s close branch) should target\\n/// when the cursor is on `line`.\\n///\\n/// If any open fold *starts* at `line`, the user is positioned on\\n/// the line that opens one or more folds (e.g. the `let len = if\\n/// cond {` line that simultaneously opens the let_declaration, the\\n/// if_expression, and the then-block). The active buffer is tagged `(current)` in the\\n/// marginalia and floated to the bottom so the picker's\\n/// initial-selected row lands on the alternate buffer (vim's\\n/// `:b<CR>` shortcut).\\npub(crate) fn raw_buffer_candidates(\\n    registry: &BufferRegistry,\\n    active: BufferId,\\n) -> Vec<(lattice_completion::RawCandidate, crate::picker::RoutingPayload)> {\\n    let mut ids = registry.sorted_ids();\\n    ids.sort_by_key(|id| (*id == active, *id));\\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(ids.len());\\n    for id in ids {\\n        let Some(entry) = registry.get(id) else {\\n            continue;\\n        };\\n        let active_marker = if id == active { \\\" (current)\\\" } else { \\\"\\\" };\\n        let (body, kind_label) = match &entry.data {\\n            BufferData::Document(d) => {\\n                let path = d\\n                    .handle\\n                    .path()\\n                    .map(|p| p.display().to_string())\\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \\\"[no name]\\\".to_string());\\n                let dirty = if d.handle.dirty() { \\\" [+]\\\" } else { \\\"\\\" };\\n                (\\n                    format!(\\\"#{:<3} {path}{dirty}\\\", id.0),\\n                    format!(\\\"doc{active_marker}\\\"),\\n                )\\n            }\\n            BufferData::FileTree(t) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, t.root.display()),\\n                format!(\\\"tree{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n            BufferData::Help(h) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, h.title),\\n                format!(\\\"help{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n            BufferData::Oil(o) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, o.dir.display()),\\n                format!(\\\"oil{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n        };\\n        // `text` is the user-facing buffer id; matcher matches\\n        // against `display`. Picks the active signature\\n/// (server-supplied `active_signature` index, default 0) and\\n/// inlines the active parameter's documentation when present.\\n/// Returns the empty string when the response carries no\\n/// signatures.\\npub(crate) fn signature_help_to_markdown(sh: &lsp_types::SignatureHelp) -> String {\\n    if sh.signatures.is_empty() {\\n        return String::new();\\n    }\\n    let active_sig_idx = sh.active_signature.unwrap_or(0) as usize;\\n    let sig = sh\\n        .signatures\\n        .get(active_sig_idx)\\n        .or_else(|| sh.signatures.first())\\n        .expect(\\\"non-empty checked above\\\");\\n    let mut out = String::new();\\n    // Active signature's call form -- renders as a fenced code\\n    // block so the popup's markdown highlighter picks up\\n    // syntax highlighting (whatever language the server says\\n    // -- we don't know, so default to text).\\n    out.push_str(\\\"```text\\\\n\\\");\\n    out.push_str(&sig.label);\\n    out.push_str(\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\");\\n    // Parameter highlight: append a short note pointing at the\\n    // active parameter's name. We pull the placeholder when\\n/// present, else `None` so the App's caller can fall back to\\n/// the heuristic.\\npub(crate) fn prepare_rename_placeholder(\\n    resp: &lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse,\\n) -> Option<String> {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::RangeWithPlaceholder { placeholder, .. } => {\\n            Some(placeholder.clone())\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::Range(_) => None,\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::DefaultBehavior { .. } => None,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `WorkspaceEdit` into a per-file\\n/// `Vec<(Uri, Vec<TextEdit>)>`. On miss the echo\\n    /// lists running actor ids so the user sees what's available\\n    /// instead of a phantom-toggle that goes nowhere.\\n    pub fn do_toggle_lsp_trace(&mut self, name: &str) {\\n        let resolved = self.resolve_server_id(name);\\n        let Some(server_id) = resolved else {\\n            let running = self.running_server_ids();\\n            let listing = if running.is_empty() {\\n                \\\"no LSP servers running\\\".to_string()\\n            } else {\\n                format!(\\\"running: {}\\\", running.join(\\\", \\\"))\\n            };\\n            self.set_message(\\n                EchoLevel::Error,\\n                format!(\\\"lsp-trace: no server matches {name:?} ({listing})\\\"),\\n            );\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let id: std::sync::Arc<str> = std::sync::Arc::from(server_id.as_str());\\n        let now_on = self.lsp_logger.toggle_trace(id);\\n        let label = if now_on { \\\"on\\\" } else { \\\"off\\\" };\\n        let alias_note = if server_id != name {\\n            format!(\\\" (resolved {name:?} -> {server_id:?})\\\")\\n        } else {\\n            String::new()\\n        };\\n        self.set_message(\\n            EchoLevel::Info,\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"lsp-trace {server_id}: {label}{alias_note} (use :lsp-trace-log {server_id} to view)\\\"\\n            ),\\n        );\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Resolve a user-supplied server name to a canonical server\\n    /// id. full restart-with-\\n    /// backoff lands in 4.4.\\n    pub fn do_lsp_restart(&mut self, server_id: &str) {\\n        self.set_message(\\n            EchoLevel::Info,\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"lsp-restart {}: supervisor restart wiring lands in 4.4\\\",\\n                server_id\\n            ),\\n        );\\n    }\\n\\n    /// `:lsp-log-level [server] <level>` -- set the subsystem\\n    /// default min level (when no server) or a per-server\\n    /// override.\\n    pub fn do_set_lsp_log_level(&mut self, server_id: Option<&str>, level: &str) {\\n        let Some(parsed) = lattice_lsp::LogLevel::parse(level) else {\\n            self.set_message(\\n                EchoLevel::Error,\\n                format!(\\n                    \\\"unknown log level {level:?};  self.publish_document_changed();\\n            for edit in &edits_for_lsp {\\n                self.lsp_record_edit(self.document_buffer_id, edit);\\n            }\\n        }\\n        result\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn undo_blocking(&self) -> Result<Vec<AppliedEdit>, RuntimeError> {\\n        let result = block_on(self.document.undo());\\n        if result.is_ok() {\\n            self.publish_document_changed();\\n        }\\n        result\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn redo_blocking(&self) -> Result<Vec<AppliedEdit>, RuntimeError> {\\n        let result = When the\\n    /// server requested `includeText`, attach the post-save\\n    /// text from the rope.\\n    fn fire_did_save_notifications(&self) {\\n        let Some(uri) = self.buffer_uris.get(&self.document_buffer_id) else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let lsp = self.lsp.clone();\\n        let uri = uri.clone();\\n        let handles = match lsp.try_lock() {\\n            Ok(g) => g.servers_for(&uri),\\n            Err(_) => return,\\n        };\\n        let snap = self.document.snapshot();\\n        let full_text = snap.buffer.as_string();\\n        for h in handles {\\n            let caps = h.capabilities();\\n            if !caps.wants_did_save() {\\n                continue;\\n            }\\n            let text = if caps.did_save_include_text() {\\n                Some(full_text.clone())\\n            } else {\\n                None\\n            };\\n            let params = lsp_types::DidSaveTextDocumentParams {\\n                text_document: lsp_types::TextDocumentIdentifier {\\n                    uri: uri.clone(),\\n                },\\n                text,\\n            };\\n            let _ = h.did_save(params);\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn save_as_blocking(&self, path: std::path::PathBuf) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {\\n        let snap = self.document.snapshot();\\n        self.event_bus.publish(Event::BeforeSave {\\n            id: snap.id,\\n            path: path.clone(),\\n        });\\n        let result = block_on(self.document.save_as(path.clone()));\\n        if result.is_ok() {\\n            self.event_bus\\n                .publish(Event::DocumentSaved { id: snap.id, path });\\n        }\\n        result\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn set_selections_blocking(&self, selections: SelectionSet) {\\n        // SetSelections only fails on actor-gone; ignore the\\n        // Result (post-shutdown nothing meaningful to do).\\n        let _ = block_on(self.document.set_selections(selections));\\n        self.publish_selections_changed();\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Build + publish [`Event::DocumentChanged`] from the current\\n    /// snapshot. The plumbing is in place for a\\n    /// future runtime that reads input on a separate task and flips\\n    /// the dispatch token on Esc; see `dispatch_with_cancel` on\\n    /// [`DocumentHandle`].\\n    pub fn dispatch_blocking(&self, invocation: CommandInvocation) -> Result<Effect, RuntimeError> {\\n        block_on(self.document.dispatch_with_cancel(\\n            invocation,\\n            self.cursor,\\n            CancellationToken::never(),\\n        ))\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn apply(&mut self, action: Action) {\\n        // Snapshot pre-dispatch state for the State-A hover\\n        // auto-dismiss hook below: while a hover popup is shown\\n        // and focus is still on the main buffer, any motion that\\n        // changes the doc cursor closes the popup -- the popup\\n        // is anchored to the symbol the user pressed `K` on, so\\n        // a cursor motion makes it stale. Once the user has\\n        // pressed `K` again to *focus into* the popup (State B,\\n        // active_buffer == Help), this auto-dismiss is skipped:\\n        // motions there move the popup's cursor, not the doc's.\\n        let pre_active = self.active_buffer;\\n        let pre_cursor = self.cursor;\\n        let popup_in_state_a = self.help_buffer.is_some()\\n            && self.prev_pane_for_help.is_none()\\n            && pre_active == BufferKind::Document;\\n        // While a macro recording is in flight, capture every Action\\n        // EXCEPT the recording-management ones themselves (otherwise the\\n        // recording would include \\\"stop recording\\\" or recurse on play).\\n        if let Some(rec) = self.macro_recording.as_mut()\\n            && !matches!(\\n                action,\\n                Action::StartMacroRecord(_)\\n                    | Action::StopMacroRecord\\n                    | Action::PlayMacro(_)\\n                    | Action::PlayLastMacro\\n            )\\n        {\\n            rec.actions.push(action.clone());\\n        }\\n        // Pending lifecycle: any action that *resolves* (i.e. isn't\\n        // itself SetPending) consumes the pending state. Maps the active\\n    /// document's filename extension to a language string the\\n    /// snippet registry indexes by (e.g. `\\\"rs\\\"` -> `\\\"rust\\\"`).\\n    /// Falls back to the empty string when no path is set\\n    /// (the registry's `\\\"*\\\"` any-language pack still applies).\\n    fn active_language_id(&self) -> String {\\n        let snap = self.document.snapshot();\\n        let Some(path) = snap.path.as_ref() else {\\n            return String::new();\\n        };\\n        match path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) {\\n            Some(\\\"rs\\\") => \\\"rust\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"py\\\") => \\\"python\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"go\\\") => \\\"go\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"js\\\") | Some(\\\"jsx\\\") | Some(\\\"mjs\\\") | Some(\\\"cjs\\\") => {\\n                \\\"javascript\\\".into()\\n            }\\n            Some(\\\"ts\\\") | Some(\\\"tsx\\\") => \\\"typescript\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"c\\\") | Some(\\\"h\\\") => \\\"c\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"cc\\\") | Some(\\\"cpp\\\") | Some(\\\"cxx\\\") | Some(\\\"hpp\\\") | Some(\\\"hxx\\\") => {\\n                \\\"cpp\\\".into()\\n            }\\n            Some(\\\"md\\\") => \\\"markdown\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"toml\\\") => \\\"toml\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"yaml\\\") | Some(\\\"yml\\\") => \\\"yaml\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"json\\\") => \\\"json\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"sh\\\") => \\\"shellscript\\\".into(),\\n            Some(\\\"lua\\\") => \\\"lua\\\".into(),\\n            Some(other) => other.to_string(),\\n            None => String::new(),\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Look up the snippet meta sidecar entry for a candidate,\\n    /// when it's a snippet-sourced one. Returns `None` for\\n    /// non-snippet candidates.\\n    pub(crate) fn snippet_meta_for(\\n        &self,\\n        candidate: &lattice_completion::RenderedCandidate,\\n    ) -> Option<&SnippetCandidateMeta> {\\n        let lattice_completion::CandidateData::Extension { kind_id, payload } =\\n            &candidate.raw.data\\n        else {\\n            return None;\\n        };\\n        if *kind_id != SNIPPET_COMPLETION_KIND_ID {\\n            return None;\\n        }\\n        if payload.len() != 4 {\\n            return None;\\n        }\\n        let idx = u32::from_le_bytes([\\n            payload[0],\\n            payload[1],\\n            payload[2],\\n            payload[3],\\n        ]) as usize;\\n        self.insert_completion_snippet_meta.get(idx)\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Path-completion sync producer (Phase 4.2.g.6 (2/2)).\\n    /// Walks the directory referenced by the partial path\\n    /// the user has typed inside the active string literal and\\n    /// emits one candidate per filesystem entry (capped at 200,\\n    /// hidden / ignored entries skipped, directories carry a\\n    /// trailing `/`). Resolves relative paths against the\\n    /// active document's parent directory; falls back to\\n    /// `std::env::current_dir()` for unsaved buffers.\\n    fn populate_path_completion(\\n        &mut self,\\n        state: &mut lattice_completion::InsertCompletionState,\\n    ) {\\n        const MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 200;\\n        // Hardcoded ignore set for v1; `.gitignore` integration\\n        // queues for a follow-up (needs the `ignore` crate +\\n        // the workspace-root resolution we already do for the\\n        // config loader).\\n        const IGNORE_NAMES: &[&str] = &[\\\".git\\\", \\\"node_modules\\\", \\\"target\\\", \\\"dist\\\"];\\n\\n        let snap = self.document.snapshot();\\n        let line_text = snap.buffer.line(state.cursor.line).unwrap_or_default();\\n        let line_bytes = line_text.as_bytes();\\n        let cursor_in_line = (state.cursor.byte as usize).min(line_bytes.len());\\n        // Walk back over path bytes (NOT stopping at `/`) to\\n        // recover the full partial path the user has typed\\n        // inside the string literal. The trigger anchor stops\\n        // at `/` so the popup-supplied filename only replaces\\n        // the tail; here we want the full thing so we know\\n        // *which* directory to walk.\\n        let mut path_start = cursor_in_line;\\n        while path_start > 0 {\\n            let b = line_bytes[path_start - 1];\\n            if b == b'/' || is_path_byte(b) {\\n                path_start -= 1;\\n            } else {\\n                break;\\n            }\\n        }\\n        let partial: &str = &line_text[path_start..cursor_in_line];\\n        // Split partial at the last `/` (boundary between dir\\n        // and the filename prefix).\\n        let dir_part = match partial.rfind('/') {\\n            Some(i) => &partial[..=i], // keep trailing slash\\n            None => \\\"\\\",\\n        };\\n        let base_dir: std::path::PathBuf = if dir_part.starts_with('/') {\\n            std::path::PathBuf::from(dir_part)\\n        } else {\\n            let buffer_dir = snap\\n                .path\\n                .as_ref()\\n                .and_then(|p| p.parent().map(|p| p.to_path_buf()));\\n            let base = buffer_dir\\n                .or_else(|| std::env::current_dir().ok())\\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| std::path::PathBuf::from(\\\".\\\"));\\n            if dir_part.is_empty() {\\n                base\\n            } else {\\n                base.join(dir_part)\\n            }\\n        };\\n\\n        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&base_dir) {\\n            Ok(it) => it,\\n            Err(_) => return, // directory unreadable / missing; popup stays empty\\n        };\\n        let path_id = lattice_completion::SourceId::new(\\n            lattice_completion::PATH_SOURCE_ID,\\n        );\\n        let mut emitted = 0;\\n        for entry in entries.flatten() {\\n            if emitted >= MAX_ENTRIES {\\n                break;\\n            }\\n            let name_os = entry.file_name();\\n            let Some(name) = name_os.to_str() else { continue };\\n            if name.starts_with('.') {\\n                // Skip hidden entries by default. Half-popup-height jump\\n    /// per press; clamps at the body's last visible line.\\n    pub fn do_completion_docs_scroll_down(&mut self) {\\n        if let Some(state) = self.insert_completion.as_mut() {\\n            if let Some(doc) = state.doc_popup.as_mut() {\\n                doc.scroll = doc.scroll.saturating_add(8);\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Page the docs popup body backward (`<C-b>` inside the\\n    /// completion-popup minor mode).\\n    pub fn do_completion_docs_scroll_up(&mut self) {\\n        if let Some(state) = self.insert_completion.as_mut() {\\n            if let Some(doc) = state.doc_popup.as_mut() {\\n                doc.scroll = doc.scroll.saturating_sub(8);\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// When the focused candidate changes (next / prev /\\n    /// refilter pinning), re-target the docs popup. If the\\n    /// popup is open AND `for_index` no longer matches\\n    /// `selected`, re-derive the body and (when needed) fire\\n    /// a fresh `completionItem/resolve`.\\n    fn refresh_docs_popup_for_selection(&mut self) {\\n        let docs_open = self\\n            .insert_completion\\n            .as_ref()\\n            .map(|s| s.doc_popup.is_some())\\n            .unwrap_or(false);\\n        if !docs_open {\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        let new_index = self\\n            .insert_completion\\n            .as_ref()\\n            .map(|s| s.selected)\\n            .unwrap_or(0);\\n        let body = self.docs_body_for_selected();\\n        let needs_resolve = body.is_none() && self.selected_needs_resolve();\\n        if let Some(state) = self.insert_completion.as_mut() {\\n            if let Some(doc) = state.doc_popup.as_mut() {\\n                doc.for_index = new_index;\\n                doc.scroll = 0;\\n                doc.body = body;\\n            }\\n        }\\n        if needs_resolve {\\n            self.do_completion_resolve_focused();\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Accept the focused candidate. The active buffer is tagged `(current)` in the\\n/// marginalia and floated to the bottom so the picker's\\n/// initial-selected row lands on the alternate buffer (vim's\\n/// `:b<CR>` shortcut).\\npub(crate) fn raw_buffer_candidates(\\n    registry: &BufferRegistry,\\n    active: BufferId,\\n) -> Vec<(lattice_completion::RawCandidate, crate::picker::RoutingPayload)> {\\n    let mut ids = registry.sorted_ids();\\n    ids.sort_by_key(|id| (*id == active, *id));\\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(ids.len());\\n    for id in ids {\\n        let Some(entry) = registry.get(id) else {\\n            continue;\\n        };\\n        let active_marker = if id == active { \\\" (current)\\\" } else { \\\"\\\" };\\n        let (body, kind_label) = match &entry.data {\\n            BufferData::Document(d) => {\\n                let path = d\\n                    .handle\\n                    .path()\\n                    .map(|p| p.display().to_string())\\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \\\"[no name]\\\".to_string());\\n                let dirty = if d.handle.dirty() { \\\" [+]\\\" } else { \\\"\\\" };\\n                (\\n                    format!(\\\"#{:<3} {path}{dirty}\\\", id.0),\\n                    format!(\\\"doc{active_marker}\\\"),\\n                )\\n            }\\n            BufferData::FileTree(t) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, t.root.display()),\\n                format!(\\\"tree{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n            BufferData::Help(h) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, h.title),\\n                format!(\\\"help{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n            BufferData::Oil(o) => (\\n                format!(\\\"#{:<3} {}\\\", id.0, o.dir.display()),\\n                format!(\\\"oil{active_marker}\\\"),\\n            ),\\n        };\\n        // `text` is the user-facing buffer id; matcher matches\\n        // against `display`. For 4.2.b utf-16 is correct\\n/// for every server we care about today.\\n/// Render an LSP `SignatureHelp` response into a markdown body\\n/// the popup renderer can display. Picks the active signature\\n/// (server-supplied `active_signature` index, default 0) and\\n/// inlines the active parameter's documentation when present.\\n/// Returns the empty string when the response carries no\\n/// signatures.\\npub(crate) fn signature_help_to_markdown(sh: &lsp_types::SignatureHelp) -> String {\\n    if sh.signatures.is_empty() {\\n        return String::new();\\n    }\\n    let active_sig_idx = sh.active_signature.unwrap_or(0) as usize;\\n    let sig = sh\\n        .signatures\\n        .get(active_sig_idx)\\n        .or_else(|| sh.signatures.first())\\n        .expect(\\\"non-empty checked above\\\");\\n    let mut out = String::new();\\n    // Active signature's call form -- renders as a fenced code\\n    // block so the popup's markdown highlighter picks up\\n    // syntax highlighting (whatever language the server says\\n    // -- we don't know, so default to text).\\n    out.push_str(\\\"```text\\\\n\\\");\\n    out.push_str(&sig.label);\\n    out.push_str(\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\");\\n    // Parameter highlight: append a short note pointing at the\\n    // active parameter's name. Used by\\n/// `apply_lsp_text_edits` to convert TextEdit ranges back to\\n/// the App's `Position` shape.\\npub(crate) fn lsp_position_to_app_byte(buffer: &Buffer, line: u32, character: u32) -> u32 {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(line).unwrap_or_default();\\n    lattice_lsp::position::utf16_column_to_utf8_byte(&line_text, character)\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn app_to_lsp_position(buffer: &Buffer, p: Position) -> Option<lsp_types::Position> {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(p.line)?;\\n    let character = lattice_lsp::position::utf8_byte_to_utf16_column(&line_text, p.byte);\\n    Some(lsp_types::Position {\\n        line: p.line,\\n        character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `DocumentSymbolResponse` into our pre-rendered\\n/// `SymbolRow` shape. The legacy `Flat(Vec<SymbolInformation>)`\\n/// variant is one row per symbol with no nesting; the modern\\n/// `Nested(Vec<DocumentSymbol>)` variant carries\\n/// `children: Vec<DocumentSymbol>`, walked depth-first to\\n/// preserve outline ordering.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_document_symbol_response(\\n    resp: lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse,\\n    path: &std::path::Path,\\n    out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n) {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Flat(syms) => {\\n            for sym in syms {\\n                if let Some(row) = symbol_information_to_row(&sym) {\\n                    out.push(row);\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Nested(syms) => {\\n            fn walk(\\n                syms: Vec<lsp_types::DocumentSymbol>,\\n                path: &std::path::Path,\\n                depth: u32,\\n                out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n            ) {\\n                for sym in syms {\\n                    out.push(SymbolRow {\\n                        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n                        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n                        container: None,\\n                        depth,\\n                        path: path.to_path_buf(),\\n                        line: sym.selection_range.start.line,\\n                        col: sym.selection_range.start.character,\\n                    });\\n                    if let Some(children) = sym.children {\\n                        walk(children, path, depth + 1, out);\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            }\\n            walk(syms, path, 0, out);\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Map a flat `SymbolInformation` (legacy outline + workspace\\n/// symbol shape) into our row type. Returns `None` when the\\n/// location's URI doesn't resolve to a path.\\npub(crate) fn symbol_information_to_row(\\n    sym: &lsp_types::SymbolInformation,\\n) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&sym.location.uri)?;\\n    Some(SymbolRow {\\n        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n        container: sym.container_name.clone(),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: sym.location.range.start.line,\\n        col: sym.location.range.start.character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// Extract a placeholder string from a `PrepareRenameResponse`.\\n/// The spec gives three shapes: a Range (no placeholder, just\\n/// \\\"you can rename here\\\"), a Range+Placeholder (preferred), or\\n/// a DefaultBehavior signal (server defers to the editor's\\n/// word-under-cursor heuristic). We pull the placeholder when\\n/// present, else `None` so the App's caller can fall back to\\n/// the heuristic.\\npub(crate) fn prepare_rename_placeholder(\\n    resp: &lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse,\\n) -> Option<String> {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::RangeWithPlaceholder { placeholder, .. } => {\\n            Some(placeholder.clone())\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::Range(_) => None,\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::DefaultBehavior { .. } => None,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `WorkspaceEdit` into a per-file\\n/// `Vec<(Uri, Vec<TextEdit>)>`. One task per App; lives\\n        // for the editor's lifetime.\\n        let (flush_tx, mut flush_rx) =\\n            tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<()>();\\n        self.lsp_flush_signal = Some(flush_tx);\\n        let supervisor_clone = std::sync::Arc::clone(&self.lsp);\\n        tokio::spawn(async move {\\n            use tokio::time::{Duration, Instant, timeout_at};\\n            const DEBOUNCE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);\\n            loop {\\n                // Wait for first edit signal.\\n                if flush_rx.recv().await.is_none() {\\n                    return;\\n                }\\n                // Coalesce additional signals during the\\n                // debounce window.\\n                let deadline = Instant::now() + DEBOUNCE;\\n                loop {\\n                    match timeout_at(deadline, flush_rx.recv()).await {\\n                        Ok(Some(())) => continue,\\n                        Ok(None) => return,\\n                        Err(_) => break, // timeout -> flush\\n                    }\\n                }\\n                let mut sup = supervisor_clone.lock().await;\\n                let _ = sup.flush_all();\\n            }\\n        });\\n    }\\n\\n    // ---- LSP integration helpers ----\\n    //\\n    // The supervisor lives on the App; its open_buffer is\\n    // async so we expose a sync-side hook (record_edit /\\n    // close_buffer / flush) for tight integration with\\n    // apply_edit_blocking and do_buffer_delete, and an async\\n    // entry point ([`Self::initialize_lsp`]) for the boot\\n    // path. None for buffers\\n    /// that have no on-disk path yet (new unsaved scratch\\n    /// buffers).\\n    pub fn buffer_uri(&self, id: BufferId) -> Option<&lattice_lsp::Uri> {\\n        self.buffer_uris.get(&id)\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Notify the LSP supervisor of an edit on a buffer. Sync;\\n    /// `try_lock` because the supervisor mutex is uncontended\\n    /// during normal operation (only async open / shutdown\\n    /// paths take it for non-trivial windows). When contended\\n    /// (rare: only during `:e <path>` async open), the edit is\\n    /// dropped on the LSP side -- the editor's buffer still\\n    /// commits; the LSP layer catches up on the next edit.\\n    /// `&self` so it can be called from `apply_edit_blocking`\\n    /// without rippling `&mut self` through 44 edit call sites.\\n    pub fn lsp_record_edit(&self, buffer_id: BufferId, edit: &Edit) {\\n        let Some(uri) = self.buffer_uris.get(&buffer_id).cloned() else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        if let Ok(mut sup) = self.lsp.try_lock() {\\n            let _ = sup.record_edit(&uri, edit);\\n        }\\n        // Wake the debounce task so a `didChange` flush fires\\n        // ~50ms after this edit (modulo further edits in that\\n        // window).\\n        if let Some(tx) = self.lsp_flush_signal.as_ref() {\\n            let _ = tx.send(());\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Flush queued didChange events for a buffer immediately.\\n    /// Used by the App's debounce timer and by will-save hooks\\n    /// (4.3). `&self` for the same reason as\\n    /// [`Self::lsp_record_edit`].\\n    pub fn lsp_flush(&self, buffer_id: BufferId) {\\n        let Some(uri) = self.buffer_uris.get(&buffer_id).cloned() else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        if let Ok(mut sup) = self.lsp.try_lock() {\\n            let _ = sup.flush(&uri);\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Detach a buffer from every attached LSP server. Called\\n    /// from the bdelete path. Sends `didClose` per server +\\n    /// clears the URI's diagnostics.\\n    pub fn lsp_close_buffer(&mut self, buffer_id: BufferId) {\\n        let Some(uri) = self.buffer_uris.remove(&buffer_id) else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        if let Ok(mut sup) = self.lsp.try_lock() {\\n            let _ = sup.close_buffer(&uri);\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Queue an LSP attachment for a freshly-opened file. The\\n    /// runtime's main loop drains the queue between input\\n    /// events so `:e <path>` doesn't have to await the\\n    /// supervisor lock + handshake on the input thread.\\n    pub fn queue_lsp_open(&mut self, buffer_id: BufferId, path: std::path::PathBuf, text: String) {\\n        self.pending_lsp_opens.push((buffer_id, path, text));\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Drain the pending-LSP-open queue (async; called by the\\n    /// runtime). For each entry, takes the supervisor lock,\\n    /// awaits open_buffer, and on success records the\\n    /// BufferId → Uri mapping.\\n    pub async fn drain_pending_lsp_opens(&mut self) {\\n        let pending: Vec<_> = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_lsp_opens);\\n        for (buffer_id, path, text) in pending {\\n            let result = {\\n                let mut sup = self.lsp.lock().await;\\n                sup.open_buffer(path.clone(), text).await\\n            };\\n            match result {\\n                Ok(_handles) => {\\n                    let uri = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_from_path(&path);\\n                    self.buffer_uris.insert(buffer_id, uri);\\n                }\\n                Err(e) => {\\n                    self.lsp_logger.log(\\n                        None,\\n                        LogLevel::Warn,\\n                        lattice_lsp::LogSource::Client,\\n                        format!(\\n                            \\\"drain_pending_lsp_opens: open_buffer({}) failed: {e}\\\",\\n                            path.display()\\n                        ),\\n                    );\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    // ---- LSP diagnostic navigation (Phase 4.1.d.iv) ---------\\n\\n    /// `:diagnostics` -- open a vertico-style picker listing every\\n    /// workspace diagnostic. `<CR>` jumps to the selected entry,\\n    /// `<Esc>` dismisses, type-to-filter walks substrings against\\n    /// the rendered `path:line:col message` rows.\\n    ///\\n    /// Empty layer echoes \\\"no diagnostics\\\" so the user always\\n    /// gets feedback. The picker rows carry severity in the\\n    /// marginalia (`[E]` / `[W]` / `[I]` / `[H]`) and the\\n    /// diagnostic message as the preview text.\\n    pub fn do_list_diagnostics(&mut self) {\\n        // `:diagnostics` is a browse-style picker, not a tag-\\n        // intent drill-down -- clear any stale nav origin so a\\n        // later JumpToLspLocation accept doesn't push a phantom\\n self.set_message(EchoLevel::Info, \\\"no diagnostics\\\".to_string());\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        let mut rows: Vec<crate::picker::LspLocationRow> = Vec::new();\\n        for (uri, diags) in snapshot {\\n            let path = match lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&uri) {\\n                Some(p) => p,\\n                None => continue,\\n            };\\n            for d in diags {\\n                let sev = match d.severity {\\n                    Some(lattice_lsp::DiagnosticSeverity::ERROR) => \\\"[E]\\\",\\n Some(lattice_lsp::DiagnosticSeverity::HINT) => \\\"[H]\\\",\\n                    _ => \\\"[?]\\\",\\n                };\\n                rows.push(crate::picker::LspLocationRow {\\n                    path: path.clone(),\\n                    line: d.range.start.line,\\n                    col: d.range.start.character,\\n                    preview: crate::help::one_line(&d.message),\\n                    marginalia: sev.to_string(),\\n                });\\n            }\\n        }\\n        if rows.is_empty() {\\n            self.set_message(EchoLevel::Info, \\\"no diagnostics\\\".to_string());\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        let total = rows.len();\\n        let mut p = crate::picker::Picker::new(\\n            format!(\\\"diagnostics ({total})\\\"),\\n            crate::picker::PickerSource::LspLocations,\\n            crate::picker::PickerAction::JumpToLspLocation,\\n        );\\n        p.set_lsp_locations(rows);\\n        self.picker = Some(p);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// `]d` / `:diag-next` / `:cnext` -- move the cursor to the\\n    /// next diagnostic in the active buffer. Surface a\\n            // no-op rather than panicking if the invariant\\n            // breaks.\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        self.cursor = Position::new(next.line, next.character);\\n        self.publish_position_change();\\n    }\\n\\n    /// `[d` / `:diag-prev` / `:cprev` -- move the cursor to the\\n    /// previous diagnostic in the active buffer. Wraps to\\n    /// bottom.\\n    pub fn do_prev_diagnostic(&mut self) {\\n        let Some(uri) = self.buffer_uris.get(&self.document_buffer_id) else {\\n            self.set_message(EchoLevel::Error, \\\"no LSP attachment\\\".to_string());\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let mut diags = self.lsp_diagnostics.diagnostics_for(uri);\\n        if diags.is_empty() {\\n            self.set_message(EchoLevel::Info, \\\"no diagnostics in buffer\\\".to_string());\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        diags.sort_by_key(|d| (d.range.start.line, d.range.start.character));\\n        let cursor = self.cursor;\\n        let Some(prev) = diags\\n            .iter()\\n            .rev()\\n            .find(|d| {\\n                d.range.start.line < cursor.line\\n                    || (d.range.start.line == cursor.line\\n                        && d.range.start.character < cursor.byte)\\n            })\\n            .or_else(|| diags.last())\\n            .map(|d| d.range.start)\\n        else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        self.cursor = Position::new(prev.line, prev.character);\\n        self.publish_position_change();\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Helper: publish a position-only change event. Currently a no-op since the\\n    /// renderer reads cursor directly; reserved for future\\n    /// position-history pushes.\\n    fn publish_position_change(&self) {\\n        // 4.1.d.iv: position history hook reserved -- a real\\n        // PluginPush entry lands here when the position-history\\n        // wiring catches up.\\n    }\\n\\n    // ---- LSP introspection (Phase 4.1.g) --------------------\\n\\n    /// `:lsp-log [server]` -- open a per-server log buffer in the\\n    /// active pane.\\n    ///\\n    /// - **No arg**: open the vertico-style picker over every\\n    ///   running `(workspace, server_id)` instance. `<CR>` opens\\n    ///   `*lsp:<server>*` for the chosen row.\\n    /// - **`server` arg**: pre-filter the picker. On miss the echo\\n    /// lists running actor ids so the user sees what's available\\n    /// instead of a phantom-toggle that goes nowhere.\\n    pub fn do_toggle_lsp_trace(&mut self, name: &str) {\\n        let resolved = self.resolve_server_id(name);\\n        let Some(server_id) = resolved else {\\n            let running = self.running_server_ids();\\n            let listing = if running.is_empty() {\\n                \\\"no LSP servers running\\\".to_string()\\n            } else {\\n                format!(\\\"running: {}\\\", running.join(\\\", \\\"))\\n            };\\n            self.set_message(\\n                EchoLevel::Error,\\n                format!(\\\"lsp-trace: no server matches {name:?} ({listing})\\\"),\\n            );\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let id: std::sync::Arc<str> = std::sync::Arc::from(server_id.as_str());\\n        let now_on = self.lsp_logger.toggle_trace(id);\\n        let label = if now_on { \\\"on\\\" } else { \\\"off\\\" };\\n        let alias_note = if server_id != name {\\n            format!(\\\" (resolved {name:?} -> {server_id:?})\\\")\\n        } else {\\n            String::new()\\n        };\\n        self.set_message(\\n            EchoLevel::Info,\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"lsp-trace {server_id}: {label}{alias_note} (use :lsp-trace-log {server_id} to view)\\\"\\n            ),\\n        );\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Resolve a user-supplied server name to a canonical server\\n    /// id. self.publish_document_changed();\\n        }\\n        result\\n    }\\n\\n    pub fn redo_blocking(&self) -> Result<Vec<AppliedEdit>, RuntimeError> {\\n        let result = No-op when\\n    /// the buffer isn't currently open.\\n    fn refresh_lsp_log_buffer_subsystem(&mut self) {\\n        let Some(id) = self.buffers.help_with_title(\\\"lsp\\\") else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let new_buf = crate::help::HelpBuffer::lsp_global_log(&self.lsp_logger)\\n            .with_markdown_syntax(self.lang_registry.clone());\\n        self.replace_help_buffer_preserving_cursor(id, new_buf);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Rebuild `*lsp:<server_id>*` from the logger snapshot.\\n    fn refresh_lsp_log_buffer_per_server(&mut self, server_id: &str) {\\n        let title = format!(\\\"lsp:{server_id}\\\");\\n        let Some(id) = self.buffers.help_with_title(&title) else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let arc: std::sync::Arc<str> = std::sync::Arc::from(server_id);\\n        let new_buf = crate::help::HelpBuffer::lsp_server_log(&self.lsp_logger, &arc)\\n            .with_markdown_syntax(self.lang_registry.clone());\\n        self.replace_help_buffer_preserving_cursor(id, new_buf);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Rebuild `*lsp:<server_id>:trace*` from the logger snapshot.\\n    fn refresh_lsp_trace_buffer(&mut self, server_id: &str) {\\n        let title = format!(\\\"lsp:{server_id}:trace\\\");\\n        let Some(id) = self.buffers.help_with_title(&title) else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        let arc: std::sync::Arc<str> = std::sync::Arc::from(server_id);\\n        let new_buf = crate::help::HelpBuffer::lsp_server_trace(&self.lsp_logger, &arc)\\n            .with_markdown_syntax(self.lang_registry.clone());\\n        self.replace_help_buffer_preserving_cursor(id, new_buf);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Atomically replace a registry-tracked help buffer's body\\n    /// with `new_buf`, preserving the existing buffer id +\\n    /// cursor + scroll so the user's view stays put across the\\n    /// rebuild. Clamps cursor to the new content's line bounds.\\n    /// Also syncs `App.help_buffer` (the popup hot-path mirror)\\n    /// when it points at the same id.\\n    fn replace_help_buffer_preserving_cursor(\\n        &mut self,\\n        id: BufferId,\\n        mut new_buf: crate::help::HelpBuffer,\\n    ) {\\n        let (cur, scr) = match self.buffers.help(id) {\\n            Some(h) => (h.cursor, h.scroll),\\n            None => return,\\n        };\\n        new_buf.id = id;\\n        new_buf.cursor = cur;\\n        new_buf.scroll = scr;\\n        let line_count = new_buf.line_count() as u32;\\n        if line_count > 0 && new_buf.cursor.line >= line_count {\\n            new_buf.cursor.line = line_count - 1;\\n        }\\n        if let Some(slot) = self.buffers.help_mut(id) {\\n            *slot = new_buf;\\n        }\\n        // Sync the popup hot-path mirror when active.\\n        if self.help_buffer.as_ref().map(|h| h.id) == Some(id)\\n            && let Some(reg) = self.buffers.help(id)\\n        {\\n            self.help_buffer = Some(reg.clone());\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// `:bd[elete]` -- close the active buffer (whichever the\\n    /// active pane shows). v1 picks any other buffer to activate;\\n    /// if no others remain, the close is rejected. For document\\n    /// buffers `!` bypasses the dirty check; tree buffers are\\n    /// always read-only and skip the dirty guard.\\n    fn do_buffer_delete(&mut self, force: bool) {\\n        if self.buffers.len() <= 1 {\\n            self.set_message(\\n                EchoLevel::Error,\\n                \\\"Cannot delete the only buffer\\\".to_string(),\\n            );\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        let to_remove = self.active_pane_buffer_id();\\n        // Dirty check applies to documents only.\\n        if let Some(d) = self.buffers.document(to_remove)\\n            && !force\\n            && d.handle.dirty()\\n        {\\n            self.set_message(\\n                EchoLevel::Error,\\n                \\\"no write since last change (add ! to override)\\\".to_string(),\\n            );\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        // Pick a successor (any other buffer in id order).\\n        let ids = self.buffers.sorted_ids();\\n        let Some(successor) = ids.iter().copied().find(|id| *id != to_remove) else {\\n            return;\\n        };\\n        self.activate_buffer(successor);\\n        // Detach from LSP before dropping the buffer registry\\n        // entry so the supervisor sees the URI go away while the\\n        // BufferId is still mapped.\\n        self.lsp_close_buffer(to_remove);\\n        self.buffers.remove(to_remove);\\n        // Re-point any pane still referencing the removed buffer.\\n        let new_id = self.active_pane_buffer_id();\\n        let new_kind = self.active_buffer;\\n        for pane in self.pane_tree.leaves_mut() {\\n            if pane.buffer_id == to_remove {\\n                pane.buffer_id = new_id;\\n                pane.buffer = new_kind;\\n            }\\n        }\\n        self.set_message(EchoLevel::Info, format!(\\\"buffer #{} deleted\\\", to_remove.0));\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Switch the active pane to whatever buffer `id` references,\\n    /// regardless of kind. Document buffers route through\\n    /// [`Self::activate_document`]; tree buffers update the active\\n    /// pane + load the tree's stash; help buffers go through\\n    /// [`Self::activate_help_in_pane`] (Phase 1 wiring).\\n    pub fn activate_buffer(&mut self, id: BufferId) {\\n        let kind = match self.buffers.get(id) {\\n            Some(entry) => entry.kind(),\\n            None => {\\n                self.set_message(EchoLevel::Error, format!(\\\"buffer #{} not found\\\", id.0));\\n                return;\\n            }\\n        };\\n        match kind {\\n            BufferKind::Document => self.activate_document(id),\\n            BufferKind::FileTree => self.activate_file_tree(id),\\n            BufferKind::Help => self.activate_help_in_pane(id),\\n            BufferKind::Oil => self.activate_oil(id),\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Switch the active pane to the file-tree buffer with `id`.\\n    /// Snapshots the current active state first; the pane's\\n    /// stashed cursor / scroll load into the tree's hot fields\\n    /// via [`Self::load_active_pane`].\\n    pub fn activate_file_tree(&mut self, id: BufferId) {\\n        if self.buffers.file_tree(id).is_none() {\\n            self.set_message(EchoLevel::Error, format!(\\\"buffer #{} not a tree\\\", id.0));\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        if id == self.active_pane_buffer_id() && matches!(self.active_buffer, BufferKind::FileTree)\\n        {\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        self.snapshot_active_pane();\\n        self.snapshot_active_document();\\n        // Load the tree's stash into the App's hot-path cursor /\\n        // scroll. After this, `self.cursor` / `self.scroll` are\\n        // the tree's -- motion / scroll / search code reads /\\n        // writes them uniformly, no per-kind branches needed.\\n        let (stash_cursor, stash_scroll) = self\\n            .buffers\\n            .file_tree(id)\\n            .map(|t| (t.cursor, t.scroll as u32))\\n            .unwrap_or((Position::ZERO, 0));\\n        self.cursor = stash_cursor;\\n        self.scroll = stash_scroll;\\n        self.active_buffer = BufferKind::FileTree;\\n        let pane = self.pane_tree.active_mut();\\n        pane.buffer = BufferKind::FileTree;\\n        pane.buffer_id = id;\\n        pane.cursor = stash_cursor;\\n        pane.scroll = stash_scroll;\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Switch the active pane to the oil buffer with `id`.\\n    pub fn activate_oil(&mut self, id: BufferId) {\\n        if self.buffers.oil(id).is_none() {\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        let oil_cursor = self.buffers.oil(id).map(|o| o.cursor).unwrap_or(Position::ZERO);\\n        let oil_scroll = self.buffers.oil(id).map(|o| o.scroll).unwrap_or(0);\\n        self.active_buffer = BufferKind::Oil;\\n        let pane = self.pane_tree.active_mut();\\n        pane.buffer = BufferKind::Oil;\\n        pane.buffer_id = id;\\n        pane.cursor = oil_cursor;\\n        pane.scroll = oil_scroll as u32;\\n        self.cursor = oil_cursor;\\n        self.scroll = oil_scroll as u32;\\n        self.pending = Pending::None;\\n    }\\n\\n    /// `:set [option | option=value | nooption | option?]`.\\n    /// Parses against the shared typed-options\\n    /// [`lattice_config::ConfigRegistry`] (DESIGN.md §5.12).\\n    /// Boolean toggle / negate forms (`:set nu` / `:set nonu`),\\n    /// query (`:set foo?`), and typed assignment (`:set tabstop=4`)\\n    /// all flow through one path. Per-file `path:body` detail rides the message\\n    /// body so the user can see *which* file complained.\\n    pub fn load_persistent_config(&mut self, workspace_root: Option<&std::path::Path>) {\\n        // The structural prefixes the App / future plugin host\\n        // own. The per-language layer drains\\n        // `completion.per-language.*`; the plugin host (Phase 7)\\n        // will drain `plugin.*`. Both buckets accumulate here\\n        // without further interpretation in this slice.\\n        let prefixes = [\\\"completion.per-language\\\", \\\"plugin\\\"];\\n        let outcome = lattice_config::load_default_paths(\\n            &self.config,\\n            workspace_root,\\n            &prefixes,\\n        );\\n        // Re-derive theme + hot-path option cache after the\\n        // loader's writes. ui.* and the cached options may have\\n        // changed; missing this would leave the first frame\\n        // rendering with stale derived state.\\n        self.sync_theme_from_config();\\n        self.rebuild_option_cache();\\n        // Stash structural sections for the layers that own\\n        // them. Subsequent slices drain via\\n        // `take_pending_structural_section(prefix)`.\\n        for (k, v) in outcome.structural {\\n            self.pending_config_structural_sections.insert(k, v);\\n        }\\n        // Surface a single echo summarising loader diagnostics.\\n        // The renderer's modeline only shows the latest echo,\\n        // so multi-warn configs collapse into \\\"<count> issues\\n        // (first: <body>)\\\". Severity is the max across the run.\\n        if outcome.messages.is_empty() {\\n            return;\\n        }\\n        let max_level = outcome\\n            .messages\\n            .iter()\\n            .map(|m| m.level)\\n            .max_by_key(|l| match l {\\n                lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Error => 1,\\n                lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Warning => 0,\\n            })\\n            .unwrap_or(lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Warning);\\n        let echo_level = match max_level {\\n            lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Error => EchoLevel::Error,\\n            lattice_config::LoadMessageLevel::Warning => EchoLevel::Warn,\\n        };\\n        let count = outcome.messages.len();\\n        let first = &outcome.messages[0];\\n        let body = if count == 1 {\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"config: {}: {}\\\",\\n                first.source.display(),\\n                first.body,\\n            )\\n        } else {\\n            format!(\\n                \\\"config: {count} issues (first: {}: {})\\\",\\n                first.source.display(),\\n                first.body,\\n            )\\n        };\\n        self.set_message(echo_level, body);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Drain every `completion.per-language.<lang>` structural\\n    /// section the loader bucketed and merge each into\\n    /// `self.per_language_completion`. Per-key TOML wins over\\n    /// the spec defaults seeded at `App::new`; unset keys leave\\n    /// the default in place.\\n    ///\\n    /// Called by the runtime startup right after\\n    /// `load_persistent_config` finishes. Per-key parse warnings collapse\\n    /// into a single echo at `Warn` level the same way the\\n    /// loader's other diagnostics do.\\n    pub fn apply_per_language_toml_overrides(&mut self) {\\n        let paths = self.pending_structural_section_paths(\\\"completion.per-language\\\");\\n        let mut warnings: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\\n        for path in paths {\\n            let lang = match path.strip_prefix(\\\"completion.per-language.\\\") {\\n                Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => s.to_string(),\\n                _ => continue,\\n            };\\n            let Some(table) = self.take_pending_structural_section(&path) else {\\n                continue;\\n            };\\n            let parsed = parse_per_language_overrides_table(&path, &table, &mut warnings);\\n            self.per_language_completion\\n                .entry(lang)\\n                .or_default()\\n                .merge(parsed);\\n        }\\n        if !warnings.is_empty() {\\n            let count = warnings.len();\\n            let body = if count == 1 {\\n                format!(\\\"config: {}\\\", warnings[0])\\n            } else {\\n                format!(\\\"config: {count} per-language warnings (first: {})\\\", warnings[0])\\n            };\\n            self.set_message(EchoLevel::Warn, body);\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Effective completion config for `language` -- per-language\\n    /// override lays over the global typed option which lays\\n    /// over the spec fallback. Removes it\\n    /// from `pending_config_structural_sections`; subsequent\\n    /// drains return `None`. Used by the per-language /\\n    /// plugin-host layers to consume their TOML config without\\n    /// leaving stale entries behind.\\n    pub fn take_pending_structural_section(\\n        &mut self,\\n        full_path: &str,\\n    ) -> Option<toml::Table> {\\n        self.pending_config_structural_sections.remove(full_path)\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Iterate the dotted paths of every pending structural\\n    /// section whose path starts with `namespace.` (e.g.\\n    /// `\\\"completion.per-language\\\"` returns the language ids).\\n    /// Returned as owned `String`s to keep the borrow short --\\n    /// callers typically follow up with\\n    /// `take_pending_structural_section(full)` mutating the map.\\n    pub fn pending_structural_section_paths(\\n        &self,\\n        namespace: &str,\\n    ) -> Vec<String> {\\n        let prefix = format!(\\\"{namespace}.\\\");\\n        self.pending_config_structural_sections\\n            .keys()\\n            .filter(|k| k.starts_with(&prefix))\\n            .cloned()\\n            .collect()\\n    }\\n\\n    fn do_set(&mut self, option: &str) {\\n        let echo = match self.config.parse_and_set_command(option) {\\n            Ok(echo) => echo,\\n            Err(err) => {\\n                self.set_message(EchoLevel::Error, err.to_string());\\n                return;\\n            }\\n        };\\n        // Drain any cascade events the set just enqueued so the\\n        // user sees the side effects (recompute folds, theme\\n        // refresh, ...) before the next frame draws. The runtime's\\n        // main_loop also drains once per iteration as a backstop\\n        // for writes that originate outside the keystroke path\\n        // (plugin tasks, future LSP-driven config writes).\\n        self.drain_option_changes();\\n        self.set_message(EchoLevel::Info, echo);\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Drain queued [`Event::OptionChanged`] events from the App's\\n    /// own bus subscription and apply per-option cascades on the\\n    /// App's main thread.\\n    ///\\n    /// Why a channel and not a callback: typed-option writes can\\n    /// originate from anywhere -- the cmdline, plugin tasks\\n    /// (Phase 7), the customize buffer view (post-1.0), or future\\n    /// LSP-driven config writes. The publisher closure on the\\n    /// registry runs *on the calling thread*, which may not be\\n    /// the App's.
